paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relationship between training time and loss for two different models, Vanilla Transformer and SepLLM. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250000, with tick marks every 50000 units. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” and has a linear scale ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick marks at 0.10 intervals.  

The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with triangular markers. Starting at a value of approximately 2.73 at a training time of 0 seconds, the line declines to approximately 2.52 at a training time of 250000 seconds, with a relatively steeper decline in the first 50000 seconds, then flattening out.  

The “SepLLM” model is represented by a red line with circular markers. Beginning at approximately 2.71 at a training time of 0 seconds, the line declines to approximately 2.50 at a training time of 250000 seconds, with a steeper decline in the first 50000 seconds and then a more gradual rate of decline thereafter. A horizontal green dashed line is present at a y-value of 2.50, spanning the entire x-axis.
